title: Wen't a little overboard with the cloud system
author: Oli4K
selftext:
The last few weeks I spent some time and credits on getting the clouds for my flight sim right. It never got to a point that looked convincing and performance was horrible. At first my idea was to generate cumulus clouds as indicators for thermals. Basically a few lobes and some ray marching. The overall look never seemed natural or convincing, so I figured I should start over and create some sort of integrated system. My agents loved that approach and scope creep set in quickly. The minions wanted to turn it into a full-blown scientific meteo and cloud simulation suite, but refused to render any good looking clouds. Yesterday I let Fable 5.2 tie all the loose ends together and for the first time I got to see some results. So far I'm pretty impressed.

The video shows a few presets with sudden changes, but it is intended to be a dynamic system.

Sky exists separately from the camera. Landscape and terrain (height, heat, humidity) feed a world-fixed atmospheric model: average fields for wind, temperature and humidity, plus loose ascents that start dry and become cumulus as soon as they condense. Low cloud cover comes from the same state.

Flight sim and renderer read the same snapshot so thermals you feel while flying are visible by 'reading' the clouds. Pixels and shadow maps do not write back. Only the water and the cover in the model do so, slowed down through the bottom.

Detail is only calculated from the camera. Far away, the rough state remains. The same seed and time give the same return the same sky, even if you fly away and come back.

It's no CFD system and doesn't do weather forecast: it is a reduced model for gliding, in which convection, gradient wind and clouds come from one budget.

On my MacBook Pro M2 it runs between 120 fps fullscreen in the lowest performance setting, down to 20 fps on the highest quality. The video was recorded with the balanced setting on, running at over 100 fps. No further optimisation has been done yet.  
  
I'm pretty happy with the results so far and prefer it over the random noise based alternatives I have tried. Next step is to integrate it into the flight sim.

replies.author: Oli4K
replies.body: Can you elaborate on what you mean with even lower halves? I do see what you mean with the snowy look. I have been focusing on coverage and shape. The cloud deck is also a bit too homogeneous now, which is something I’m going to work on next together with the more cloud-like softness.
